faq: Which app frameworks do you work with?
Swift, Kotlin, React Native, Flutter, React and Next.js are all fine. We add the AI feature in the style of your existing code. Tell us your stack in the form and we confirm before starting.
Will my users' data go to the AI provider?

Only what the feature needs, and we tell you exactly what is sent. We help you write a short privacy note and avoid sending personal details where the feature does not need them. You stay responsible for your privacy policy.
Do you need my source code?
Yes, access through your own repository as a collaborator. We work on a branch, so your main code stays untouched until you approve the merge.
Will the app stores accept AI features?
We build to Apple and Google rules, including clear labelling of AI content and a way to report bad output. Store review decisions are theirs, so we cannot promise approval.

desc:
AI features for mobile and web apps, such as in-app chat, summaries, smart suggestions and voice notes turned into text, can make an existing product more useful. Ecom Swift LLC adds them securely, tests on real devices and delivers the code to your own repository.

## What are AI features for mobile and web apps?

They are product features that call an AI model to do a task inside your app. A user taps a button and gets a summary of a long note. They type a question and get a reply from an in-app assistant. They record a voice memo and see it as text. The model itself runs on a provider's servers, and your app talks to it through a secure link.

The feature is only as good as the design around it: what the screen shows while it thinks, what happens when it fails and how much each user may use.

## Why the build matters more than the model

Calling an AI service from a sample script is easy. Shipping it inside an app that real people use is harder. Keys must be kept out of the app code, since anything inside a downloadable app can be extracted. Responses take seconds, so screens need clear loading states. Networks drop, providers return errors and users send unexpected input.

When these cases are ignored, the feature feels broken even though the model works. A careful build makes the AI part feel like a normal, dependable part of the product.

## How it affects your app

A well-placed AI feature saves users effort at the exact moment they need it. A summary shortens a reading task. A suggestion removes a blank-page problem. Chat answers a question without leaving the screen. Features like these can raise how often people open the app and how long they stay, though results depend on whether the feature solves a real need.

Usage limits protect your costs. Each request has a price, so free and paid users often get different allowances.

## What a good app integration includes

- A small server link between your app and the AI provider, so keys never ship inside the app.
- A designed screen for the feature, matching your existing visual style.
- Clear loading, error and offline states.
- Input checks that stop empty or oversized requests.
- Saved chat or result history, where it helps the user.
- Per-user limits, and tiers for free and paid users.
- Event tracking, so you can see how each feature is used.
- Testing on real devices and browsers rather than only on a simulator.
- Code delivered to your repository with a short guide.
- A build prepared for your normal release steps and store review.

## What we do

We begin with your codebase and the feature you want. We design the screen, build the server link, connect the model and test on real devices, then push the work to your repository on a branch you can review.

The Basic package adds one feature and one screen. The Standard package covers two features, more screens, saved history and complete error states. The Premium package adds usage tiers, event tracking, a release-ready build and a handover call. We work with common mobile and web frameworks, and we tell you early if yours needs extra care.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide exactly what the feature does for the user before building it.
- Tell users when they are talking to an AI and what is sent to the provider.
- Keep a visible way to report a poor answer.
- Set usage limits from day one.
- Test on older and smaller devices, not only your own phone.

**Avoid:**
- Putting provider keys inside the app package.
- Blocking the whole screen while a reply loads.
- Sending more user data to the provider than the feature needs.
- Adding AI to every screen at once.
- Assuming an app store will approve a feature without checking its current guidelines.

## Who it is for

A founder with a note-taking app wants automatic summaries. A company with a customer app wants an in-app assistant for common questions. A developer with a web tool wants photo tagging and does not want to design the server side alone.

## What we need from you

We need access to the repository, as a collaborator or developer user on your code host, plus a test build or staging site and a description of the feature. If you have a provider account, add us as a team member, or we help you set one up in your name. We never ask for passwords. Store approval remains decided by the store, and we prepare the build to meet its rules.
